# BGET — Personal Invite Message

Use this when inviting someone **you actually know** and have seen handle
something well. Do not send this to strangers. Do not send it in bulk.

---

## The message (adapt, don't recite)

> Hey {name} — I'm starting something and you were one of the first people
> I thought of.
>
> It's called **BGET** — Build, Grow, Evolve, Together. Basically a small
> community of people who are ambitious but not jerks: builders, thinkers,
> people who care about what they're doing and how they do it. The idea is
> capability *with* character.
>
> It's tiny right now — a handful of people — and I'm keeping it that way on
> purpose for now. I'd rather have ten people I'd actually want to work with
> than a thousand I'd have to manage.
>
> The reason I thought of you: {specific, honest reason — "you explained X to me
> and didn't make me feel stupid", "you shipped that project when everyone else
> dropped off", "you argue fairly, which is rare"}.
>
> No pressure at all — but if that sounds like your kind of room, here's the
> server: {link}. Read the manifesto first; if it doesn't resonate, it's
> genuinely not for you, and that's fine.
>
> What we actually do: weekly build nights where we build together, a weekly
> deep dive where someone presents something they're obsessed with, and a
> monthly thing where we go do something measurable in the real world.
>
> Anyway — no pitch. Just thought of you.

---

## Why this works

| Element | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| "You were one of the first people I thought of" | Personal, not broadcast |
| "ambitious but not jerks" | Says the differentiator plainly |
| "ten people I'd actually want to work with" | Signals quality filter; makes joining feel selective |
| **Specific honest reason** | The whole message lives or dies here — make it true |
| "if it doesn't resonate, it's not for you" | Gives an out; raises trust, paradoxically raises acceptance |
| Concrete activities | Proof it's not just vibes |
| "No pitch" | Because you already pitched a little — naming it disarms |

---

## Rules

1. **Never** send this to someone you've only seen online and never interacted with.
   Comment on their work first, over weeks, then invite.
2. **One message, one person.** No copy-paste blasts, no BCC, no "hey everyone".
3. **If they decline, respond well.** "All good — staying in touch either way."
   The person you handle a "no" from gracefully is often the person who joins in six months.
4. **Log it** in `roster.md`: name, date invited, outcome, follow-up date.
5. **After they join:** you reply to their introduction *yourself*, within 24h.
   They came because of you. Don't delegate the first impression.

---

## Referral message (for members to use after they're confirmed)

> I've been in a community called BGET for a few months and it's genuinely
> different — small, no self-promo culture, people actually help each other
> and actually ship things.
>
> They're being careful about who comes in, so there's a short application and
> a quick chat. I can vouch that it's worth it.
>
> Want me to pass your name along? {link}

**Why referrals are your best growth channel:** the referrer stakes their own
reputation, so the filter applies itself. You never have to lower the bar —
your members pre-select for it.
